security.lockDescription: Ask for a password before this terminal can be used on this device.
security.biometricUnlockDescription: Open the lock screen with this device's own unlock — Face ID, Touch ID, a fingerprint, Windows Hello — instead of typing the password.
security.biometricUnlockScreenOnly: Your password still works, and it stays the only way back in if the sensor stops recognising you.
security.biometricUnlockVaultNote: This opens the screen only. Your stored keys still ask for their own password — add a passkey to your vault below to open both with one gesture.
security.biometricUnlockCoveredByVault: Your vault already unlocks with a passkey or Touch ID, and that opens the lock screen too. A second one here would do less.
security.turnOffDescription: Enter your current password to remove the lock from this device.
security.noRecoveryWarning: There is no password recovery. If you forget it, the only way back in erases this device's data. Save it in your password manager now.
security.triggersDescription: Choose the moments the password prompt should appear.
security.triggerStartupHint: Ask for the password on a cold start.
security.triggerIdleHint: Lock after {{minutes}} minutes with no mouse or keyboard.
security.triggerPeriodicHint: Lock again after a fixed time, however busy the session is.
security.triggerWakeHint: Lock when the machine comes back from sleep.
security.triggerTradeHint: Confirm an order you place by hand or through the copilot, including auto-approved proposals. Bots are never asked.
security.protectsBody: It puts a full-screen password prompt in front of the terminal, so someone at your desk cannot click around your positions, read your balances, or place an order. It encrypts nothing: your exchange API keys and wallet keys stay exactly where they were, and anyone with your unlocked computer and some technical skill can read this app’s local data without ever seeing the prompt.
security.protectsBots: Armed bots keep trading while the terminal is locked. Locking the screen is not pausing your strategies.
security.protectsDesktop: Your password check is stored in the system keychain and never leaves this computer.
security.protectsBrowser: This build stores the password check in browser storage. Clearing site data removes the lock. The desktop app is the supported home for this.
security.lockNowDescription: Close settings and lock the terminal immediately.
security.resetConfirmBody: This erases every exchange API key, wallet key, workspace, chart layout and chat on this computer. There is no undo and no password recovery. If you are signed in, settings that sync to the cloud come back when you sign in again — API keys and wallet keys never do, because they are only ever stored here.
security.vaultDescription: Encrypt your exchange API keys and wallet keys with a password or a passkey.
security.vaultAlsoUnlocks: Any of these also unlocks the terminal lock screen — one password serves both.
security.biometricNeedsVault: Set up the vault with a password first — Touch ID is then added on top.
security.vaultRemoveLastBlocked: This is the only way into your vault. Add another before removing it.
security.vaultRemoveBiometricOnlyBlocked: Touch ID cannot be the only way in — the fingerprints on this Mac can change. Keep a password or a passkey.
security.vaultProtectsBody: With a vault, your API keys and wallet keys are stored encrypted. Someone who copies this browser profile — or this device's storage — gets ciphertext they cannot open without your password or your passkey.
security.vaultCeiling: It does not protect keys while you are using them. Anything running inside this page can ask the unlocked vault for a key, the same way the app does. The desktop app remains the recommendation for your most valuable keys.
security.vaultNoRecovery: There is no recovery. Lose every way in and the encrypted keys are gone — the only way back into the app erases this device's data.
security.vaultDesktopToggleHint: Your keys are already in the system keychain. Turn this on to add a password or a passkey on top.
security.vaultDesktopOptOutBody: Your keys go back to being protected by the system keychain alone. Nothing is deleted, and you can turn the vault back on later.
security.vaultMigrated_one: Moved 1 key you already had into the vault.
security.vaultMigrated_other: Moved {{count}} keys you already had into the vault.
security.vaultMigrationFailed: Vault setup did not finish. Your keys are still readable — open the vault to complete it.
security.vaultSharedBackoff: The vault and the lock screen share one attempt limit, so too many wrong passwords delays both.
security.vaultCliNote: The command-line tool takes API keys as arguments and never reads the vault.
security.hardLockDescription: Lock the vault, not just the screen.
security.hardLockWarning: Locks the vault, not just the screen. Live bots and automations stop trading until you unlock. Paper bots keep running.
security.hardLockConfirmBody: Live bots and automations stop trading until you unlock again. Paper bots keep running.

localOnly.title: Your keys never leave this device
localOnly.subtitle: Exactly what happens to the API keys and wallet keys you add, including what this cannot protect.
localOnly.statusDesktop: Right now: your keys sit in {{vault}}, on this computer only.
localOnly.statusDesktopVault: Right now: {{vault}}, with your own vault encrypting every key on top.
localOnly.statusBrowserVault: Right now: every key encrypted in your vault, in this browser only.
localOnly.statusBrowserNone: No vault on this browser yet. You will set one up before the first key can be saved.
localOnly.deviceBody: Your exchange API keys and wallet keys are saved on this computer and nowhere else. They are never uploaded to Pairlens: not when you sign in, not when your settings sync, not when the copilot reads a chart. There is no copy on our servers to leak.
localOnly.osBodyDesktop: They live in {{vault}}, the same protected store your system uses for its own passwords, encrypted on disk and handed out only to this app.
localOnly.osBodyDesktopVault: They live in {{vault}}, the same protected store your system uses for its own passwords. Your vault adds a layer on top: every value is sealed with AES-256-GCM before the keychain ever sees it.
localOnly.osBodyBrowser: Every value is sealed with AES-256-GCM before it touches browser storage. One data key encrypts them all, and that key is never written down in the clear.
localOnly.unlockBody: A password, stretched with 600,000 rounds of PBKDF2-SHA256; a passkey on your phone or security key; or Touch ID. Each one wraps the same data key, so you can keep more than one way in. Pairlens never receives any of them.
localOnly.openSourceTitle: Public source code — verify it yourself
localOnly.openSourceBody: Pairlens's code is public. You, a developer friend, or even an AI can read it and confirm your keys really do stay put.
localOnly.limitsRunning: While the app is open and unlocked it can read your keys. That is how it places your orders. The encryption defends a copied disk or browser profile, not a machine someone is already sitting at.
localOnly.limitsNoRecovery: There is no recovery. Lose every way in and the encrypted keys are gone for good.

desktopInvite.bannerBody: Workspaces, bots, your own indicators and four more venues.
desktopInvite.lead: Your phone carries the parts of Pairlens you want in your hand: the chart, the book, the ticket and the co-pilot. The rest of the terminal was built for a screen with room to spread out, and it is waiting for you there.

workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.body: Chart, order book, tape and co-pilot side by side, arranged once and saved. The Workspace Store has ready-made layouts you can copy in a tap.

bots.title: Bots
bots.body: Deploy a strategy to a market, backtest it first, then watch it work under the same risk limits you set here.

indicators.title: Your own indicators
indicators.body: Write chart indicators in real Python, with pip packages and a live preview beside the editor.

workflows.title: Workflows
workflows.body: Turn a signal into a chain of steps that keeps watching the market while you get on with your day.

plugins.title: Plugin Store
plugins.body: Add connectors, indicators, themes and AI providers, and decide how far each one is trusted.

keychain.title: Keys in the system keychain
keychain.body: The desktop app hands your exchange keys to macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager or the Linux secret service instead of keeping them in browser storage.

venues.title: Four more venues
venues.body: Coinbase, Gate, KuCoin and MEXC do not answer a browser. The desktop app reaches all fifteen.

background.title: Keeps running when you close it
background.body: Close the window and bots and alerts stay up, with a system notification the moment one fires.

windows.title: More than one window
windows.body: Pull a market out into a window of its own and put it on a second screen.

desktopInvite.where: Open terminal.pairlens.finance on your computer and everything above is one window away. There is a desktop app too, for macOS, Windows and Linux, and it is the one that unlocks the last four.
